subject: Post-call: Audit trace delivery checklist and sample export
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Jenkins <sara.jenkins@cardopay.com>, Lucas Moreno <lucas.m@cardopay.com>
Date: Tue, 8 Dec 2026 15:05:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap & immediate asks — CardoPay audit traces

Thanks for the call earlier. Quick recap and our asks so we can move CardoPay toward a compliance sign-off:

- Key ask from CardoPay: concrete "who/what/when" audit exports showing which authenticated user or service performed actions, the request payload metadata, model version used, and timestamp (UTC). They want an export they'd ingest into their SIEM.
- Retention: they stated a hard requirement of 13 months for audit data, with the ability to request ad-hoc longer retention for specific investigations.
- Residency: CardoPay wants EU residency for logs for EU customers; they may require a private deployment if we cannot guarantee regionally-scoped export pipelines.
- PII handling: they asked for guidance on redaction/pseudonymization of request payloads and whether we can produce redacted exports that still map request ids to internal user ids.
- Format: CardoPay prefers CSV for ingestion but asked whether JSONL with per-event schema is available.

Next steps I promised on the call:
1) Provide a short sample export (fields + 5 example rows) and a formal export schema.
2) Confirm whether we can sign exports (SHA256) and include cryptographic attestations.
3) Outline residency options and whether the hosted EU region already contains the request logs or if Private/VPC is required.
4) Schedule a 45-min technical deep-dive with Rishi and CardoPay security for next week.

I will attach a draft spec and a tiny sample in my next message. Please weigh in on feasibility re: retention & signing.

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood-audit-export-spec-v1.xlsx (spreadsheet stub), example-who-when-export.json (sample)

From: Sara Jenkins <sara.jenkins@cardopay.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Lucas Moreno <lucas.m@cardopay.com>
Date: Wed, 9 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & immediate asks — CardoPay audit traces

Hi Ben — thanks for the summary and for jumping on this quickly. A few clarifications from our security/compliance team: 

- Required fields: our auditors need (1) request_id, (2) authenticated_user_id (or service_account_id), (3) action/type (e.g., generate/embedding/rename), (4) model_identifier + version, (5) token_count (or cost-est), (6) timestamp in ISO8601 UTC, and (7) response status/code.
- Payload: actual user-provided text is PII in some flows. We need the option to have the request payload omitted or pseudonymized but still retain a deterministic mapping (request_id -> redaction token) so we can tie behavior back to the original request for investigations.
- Format & delivery: CSV is preferred for our pipeline, but we can accept gzipped JSONL. Timestamps must be UTC.
- Retention: 13 months is our baseline. For investigations we may request export snapshots retained for 3 extra months; want to understand the SLA and process for ad-hoc holds.
- Export signing: we require signed manifests for audit packages (SHA256 + signing cert). Is Redwood able to produce a signed manifest, or will we need to verify with a Redwood-supplied public key?
- Residency: EU-hosted logs are mandatory for EU customer data. Please confirm whether we can get EU-only exports without Private deployment — alternatively, outline the minimum steps & timeline for a Private/VPC option.

Two administrative items: please send the sample within 24-48 hours; and we'll need an internal contact for a security deep-dive. I can do Thu 10th 10:30-11:15 CET or Fri 11th 14:00-14:45 CET.

-Sara
Sara Jenkins
Senior Compliance Manager — CardoPay Inc.
attachments: none

Sara — thanks, very helpful.

Short answers up front: we can produce both CSV and JSONL (gzipped) exports with the fields you listed; timestamps will be in ISO8601 UTC. We can include model_identifier + version and token_count.

On pseudonymization: we can produce a deterministic hash mapping (request_id -> redaction_token) so you can join back to original requests if you hold that mapping. We do not retain raw PII in hosted exports unless the customer explicitly enables full payload retention; default hosted behavior is to exclude raw request text unless configured.

On signing: Redwood can produce a signed manifest (SHA256) for export packages and provide a public key to validate signatures. I will ask Rishi to confirm the signing certificate rotation policy and the manifest format.

Residency: our hosted EU region stores logs in-region, but the standard hosted export pipeline may stream through a global intermediary for delivery. For strict EU-only custody, we recommend Redwood Private (VPC) — Rishi, can you confirm timeline and minimum infra required for a Private deployment for CardoPay?

Attached: a short sample (example-who-when-export.json) and a draft export spec (redwood-audit-export-spec-v1.xlsx). The sample contains 5 rows and the spec defines the field names and types.

Proposed next steps:
- Rishi to confirm technical feasibility (retention mechanics, signing cert).
- Schedule the security deep-dive: Thu 10th 10:30 CET (Ben/ Rishi / CardoPay security). Please confirm if that works.
- CardoPay to share any internal encryption keys/requirements if you want envelope encryption of export bundles.

Following up with technical confirmation / implementation notes:

- Export fields: request_id, user_id (or service_account_id), action_type, model_id, model_version, token_count, bytes_in, bytes_out, response_code, user_agent, source_ip (anonymized if required), timestamp_utc. We can also surface internal node_id for debugging but recommend redacting in external packs.
- Formats: we will provide CSV (RFC4180) and JSONL (one JSON object per line). Bundles will be gzipped and accompanied by a manifest.json that includes SHA256 checksums for each file.
- Signing: we will sign the manifest with a rotating RSA2048 key and publish the verifying public key at a stable URL; we support PKCS#7 signed manifests if required.
- Retention: hosted solution can enforce retention via object lifecycle rules; 13 months default is straightforward. For ad-hoc holds we can place objects in a hold bucket for an additional configurable period (process TBD; will require signed request from CardoPay security).
- Residency: hosted EU region keeps logs in eu-west-1 (data center metadata included). To guarantee EU-only outbound exports without any global transit, Private/VPC is required. Private deployment ETA: ~4-6 weeks after order and infra provisioning; minimal requirements: two dedicated GPU nodes, VPC peering, and S3-compatible storage in-customer region. We can put together a short deployment runbook.
- PII handling: we can run a pseudonymization pipeline that replaces raw payloads with HMAC-based tokens when requested; we will provide the mapping only via secured transfer if the customer signs an NDA/PO.

I'll attach a CSV schema sample. For the deep-dive, Thu 10th 10:30 CET works for me. Ben, please confirm final attendee list and I'll prepare a short engineering deck.

Rishi
Rishi Malhotra | Senior Staff Engineer, Redwood Inference
